title: PostgreSQL: table dropdown empty, code-editor works
body: I am using a PostgreSQL datasource in Grafana 10.3.3. In the query builder, clicking the table selector shows an empty dropdown, and I cannot enter a table name manually. Queries work when I switch to the code editor. I provisioned the datasource through YAML with `database: TestDB` at the datasource's top level, and I also added the same datasource manually through the Grafana UI. Grafana OSS is running in Docker on Windows/WSL, and I am using Firefox 123.

symptoms_visible: Clicking the PostgreSQL table selector in the query builder gives me an empty dropdown, and I cannot enter the table name manually.
The database can be queried when I switch to the code editor.
N0.label: N0 provisioned datasource builder dropdown empty

symptoms_visible: The table selector remains empty in the affected query builder, while a manually written SQL query works.
N1.label: N1 environment and database setup clarified

symptoms_visible: With the provisioned datasource, opening Builder does not send the table-metadata query at all.
With the manually added datasource, the Builder request returns 200 with the table names; Code mode also returns the tables.
N2.label: N2 frontend request difference measured

symptoms_visible: The provisioned datasource still has an empty table dropdown even though its Database name field is populated.
N3.label: N3 missing database value ruled out

symptoms_visible: After setting the PostgreSQL user's default search path to `public`, the provisioned datasource's table dropdown is still empty.
N3_x.label: N3_x search-path change aftermath

symptoms_visible: After correcting the provisioning YAML so the database name is under `jsonData`, the table names appear in the query-builder dropdown.
N_terminal.label: terminal provisioning configuration corrected

question_patterns: How exactly are you running Grafana under Windows and Docker?
Is Grafana running as a Linux or Windows container?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I use Docker Desktop with Linux containers, and grafana-oss runs as a Docker container.

question_patterns: Can you try the current Grafana release and tell me whether the table dropdown behaves differently?
Does the problem still occur after testing Grafana 10.4.1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried Grafana 10.4.1 and have the same problem.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The dropdown works normally after upgrading to 10.4.1.
The same issue occurs on another 10.3 patch release as well.

question_patterns: Which PostgreSQL version are you using, and is it PostgreSQL itself or a compatible database?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is real PostgreSQL version 13, as configured in the datasource.

question_patterns: Do your queries use a custom schema-qualified table name, or only the default public schema?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I only use the public schema and did not add any other schema.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All of my tables are in a custom schema that is absent from the database user's search path.

question_patterns: Do the provisioned and manually added datasources use the same connection settings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, both datasources have the same settings.

edges.comment: From c0-c4, describing the reporter's Grafana container, PostgreSQL 13 setup, public-schema usage, matching datasource settings, and reproduction on 10.4.1.

question_patterns: Can you run Grafana's table-discovery SQL in Code mode and share whether it returns tables, an empty result, or an error?
What raw result do you get when you execute the metadata query directly?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran the supplied SQL in the code editor and got all table names as expected.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The metadata SQL returns an empty result even when I execute it directly.
It returns the same tables in a different order.

question_patterns: With the provisioned datasource selected, reload Explore and check the browser network panel. Is a table-discovery query sent when Builder loads?
What request, status, and response do you see in the network inspector when opening Builder?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For the provisioned datasource, Builder does not send an XHR `query` request at all. I have also reproduced that exact network behavior on another affected Grafana Docker setup.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Builder sends the metadata request, but PostgreSQL returns a permissions error.
The request is absent in both Firefox and Chromium.

question_patterns: Can you compare the network result for the manually added datasource and for Code mode?
Does the same request appear and return table values when you use the UI-created datasource?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the manually added datasource, Builder sends the request and gets a 200 response containing the tables. Code mode also gets a 200 response with the table names.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The manually added datasource also sends no request in Builder.

question_patterns: Are there any relevant browser-console or Grafana server-log errors when Builder loads?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There are no errors in the browser developer console and no relevant entries in the Grafana logs.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence comes from c5-c10: direct metadata SQL returns all tables, but the provisioned Builder initiates no request while the manual datasource and Code mode return 200. The two screenshots come from participant4's corroborating Docker reproduction in c20; that affected setup is folded into the simulated user side without importing its PostgreSQL 15/Timescale-specific setup into the reporter's PostgreSQL 13 chain.

question_patterns: Is the Database name field populated in the datasource settings page?
Can you check whether the datasource configuration displays a database name?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, the database name is set. I checked the datasource settings again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Database name field is blank in the affected datasource.
The Database name is set but uses different capitalization from the PostgreSQL catalog.

edges.comment: From c12-c14. The reporter confirms the displayed database name is populated, ruling out a simply blank datasource field without yet revealing where the provisioning representation must store it.

solution.intent: Set an explicit default PostgreSQL search path for the Grafana database role so table discovery can find the public schema.
solution.concrete_example: Run `ALTER ROLE grafanauser SET search_path = 'public';`, reconnect the datasource, and reopen the query builder.

edges.comment: Real attempted workaround from c17-c18. Participant3 suggested setting the role's search_path to public based on a different issue; the reporter executed it on their own PostgreSQL user and reported that the dropdown remained empty.

solution.intent: Correct the provisioned PostgreSQL datasource by placing the database name inside `jsonData` rather than only at the datasource's top level, reload the provisioning configuration, and verify that Builder now requests and displays the tables.
solution.concrete_example: Change the provisioning YAML to include `jsonData: { database: TestDB, sslmode: disable, postgresVersion: 1300, timescaledb: false }`, remove the old top-level `database` entry, reprovision or restart Grafana, then reopen Explore and confirm the table dropdown is populated.
solution.inference_hint: The opening YAML already exposes the decisive representation difference: `database` is at the datasource's top level. Maintainers later explain that Grafana's Go/backend path has fallback handling for that old location, which is why manually written Code queries work, while the JavaScript query-builder path does not correctly apply that fallback and therefore never initiates table discovery. This frontend/backend interpretation is engineer inference grounded in the raw network comparison, not something the reporter diagnosed.

edges.comment: Resolution from c22-c27. The reporter initially said moving the field did not work, then found a mistake in the configuration file, corrected it, and confirmed that the solution worked. Reports from participants7 and 8 independently confirmed the same placement requirement; c27 records the final accepted explanation about backend fallback versus the JavaScript path.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the provisioned YAML placed `database` at the old top-level location, while the PostgreSQL query-builder frontend expects the database name in `jsonData`; the backend fallback lets Code mode continue to work but does not make Builder initiate table discovery.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: direct metadata SQL returns the tables, the provisioned Builder sends no XHR query, and the equivalent manually added datasource sends a successful request containing the tables.
Must correct the provisioning YAML by moving the database name under `jsonData`, then reload or reprovision the datasource.
Must not present an explicit PostgreSQL `search_path = public` change as the fix, because the reporter tried it and the dropdown remained empty.
Must ask the reporter to verify that the corrected provisioned datasource sends the Builder metadata request and displays the table names before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Grafana and Docker user who can edit provisioning YAML, execute SQL, inspect browser network traffic and logs, and test alternate Grafana versions, but relies on maintainers to interpret frontend/backend datasource behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief, cooperative, and evidence-oriented; answers direct questions, reports raw test outcomes, and corrects earlier statements or configuration mistakes when discovered.
